title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is the middle page of a letter from Pierre Deligne to Grothendieck, signed 'Bien à toi, Pierre' on the next page. In it Deligne summarises the main theorem of complex multiplication (Shimura–Taniyama) in his own adelic formulation.

Setup (previous page). K is a CM field of degree 2g. The objects are triples (A, m, α):
- A is an abelian variety up to isogeny over Q̄ of dimension g;
- m is an action of K on A;
- α is a K⊗A_f-linear isomorphism V_{A_f}(A) ≅ K⊗A_f, a trivialisation of the adelic Tate module.

The CM type is encoded by the K–Q̄-bimodule Lie A. Its field of definition is the reflex field K' (Deligne's 'corps dual'), the field of definition of the character det Lie of R_{K/Q}G_m. Lie A descends to a K–K'-bimodule L_0. The reflex norm is δ: R_{K'/Q}G_m → R_{K/Q}G_m, k' ↦ det_K(k' | L_0).

This page:
1. K' is again CM over a totally real F'.
2. Restricted to F'^*, δ equals N_{F'/Q}. So δ kills the torus Ker(N: F'^* → G_m).
3. Consequence: let ū ∈ Gal(Q̄/K')^ab correspond under class field theory to an idèle ũ. The class of the finite part of δ(ũ) modulo K^* is well defined. The ambiguity in ũ comes from K'^*, from the connected component at infinity, and from closures of unit groups. Norm-one units of F' have finite index in the units of K', and δ kills them, so the ambiguity disappears.
4. Theorem: for u ∈ Gal(Q̄/K'), the isomorphism class of u(A, m, α) depends only on ū. It is the class of (A, m, δ(ũ)^{-1}∘α). This is the main theorem of CM restricted to Gal(Q̄/E*), in the form found in Deligne's Shimura-variety work and in Milne's notes.
5. Example, K imaginary quadratic. Elliptic curves with CM by O correspond to triples (A, m, α) with α given modulo Ô^*. The chain is: lattices T_ℓ that are O⊗Z_ℓ-stable and standard for almost all ℓ, then trivialisations α_ℓ modulo (O⊗Z_ℓ)^*.
6. The next page specialises the theorem. Gal(Q̄/K) acts through Gal(H/K) ≅ Cl(O), with σ(E) ≅ E ⊗_O 𝔞^{±1}.

Role in the dossier: Grothendieck ('Teichmülleries') was interested in the Galois action on special points of moduli of curves and abelian varieties. Deligne is supplying the standard CM description of the Galois action on CM points.
errors: No mathematical errors. Deligne himself leaves the sign convention (𝔞 versus 𝔞^{-1}) unspecified on the next page.
Statements are given without proof ('on vérifie'). For instance, δ|_{F'^*} = N_{F'/Q} follows because the reflex type restricted to F' runs over all embeddings of F' exactly once.

ideas.what: Reflex field defined as the field of definition of det Lie A (equivalently, of descent of the bimodule Lie A); reflex norm as det_K of multiplication on L_0
ideas.modern_name: Reflex field and reflex norm of a CM type
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (1961); bimodule/determinant formulation by Deligne (Variétés de Shimura, 1971; Hodge Cycles, LNM 900, 1982)
ideas.where_published: Shimura–Taniyama; Deligne LNM 900; Milne's CM notes

ideas.what: The reflex field is CM, and the reflex norm kills the norm-one torus of F', so finite idèle classes are well defined modulo K^*
ideas.modern_name: Standard lemma in the adelic main theorem of CM

ideas.what: Galois action u(A,m,α) ≅ (A,m,δ(ũ)^{-1}∘α) for u ∈ Gal(Q̄/K')
ideas.modern_name: Main theorem of complex multiplication (Shimura–Taniyama), adelic form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama; adelic form by Shimura and Deligne; extended to all of Aut(C) by Langlands, Tate, Deligne

ideas.what: CM elliptic curves by O_K correspond to isogeny classes with adelic trivialisation modulo Ô^*; class group action E ↦ E⊗_O 𝔞
ideas.modern_name: Classical CM theory of elliptic curves / Hilbert class field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kronecker, Weber, Hasse, Deuring; Serre's 'Complex multiplication' (1967)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard exposition by Deligne of the main theorem of CM, written for Grothendieck. Its only interest is historical: it documents Deligne feeding CM theory into Grothendieck's 1981–82 Teichmüller/anabelian work. It contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '(Th)' is circled in the original, marking the theorem statement with a vertical bar.
The struck-out fragment before ū reads roughly 'de' (or 'du') and is crossed out; the transcription's [-de-] is fine.
'V_{A^f}(A)' is written with a blackboard A carrying superscript f (finite adèles), i.e. V_{A_f}(A).
